notes: The 60 欠缺 IDs are all explicitly N/A or ACE_EQUIV; none fall back to the default APPLICABLE disposition.
CLOUD-001 remains APPLICABLE because its authentication-failure fail-open risk is transferable even without an Ace cloud-tasks product.
Other disposition groups already present in this global ledger belong to later tasks and are preserved here without changing their baseline state.

disposition_groups.name: external_sandbox_semantics_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace does not expose a caller-selectable ExternalSandbox mode. Existing managed and disabled modes remain governed by their own baseline IDs; adding an external-sandbox bypass is not part of the product boundary.
review_triggers: A caller-selectable already-sandboxed/external execution mode is introduced.
Any launch path starts skipping the Ace native runtime because a caller claims external isolation.

disposition_groups.name: codex_arg0_multi_identity_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace ships separate Python/Desktop/native entry points and has no Codex-style single binary whose basename selects sandbox, patch, exec, or filesystem helper identities. ARG0-002 remains APPLICABLE because its unsandboxed-write risk must be tested independently.
evidence: crew/security/launch.py and security-runtime/src/main.rs (separate Ace launch boundary)
review_triggers: Ace combines helper roles into one executable selected by argv0 or argv1.
An alias or basename starts selecting privileged helper behavior.

disposition_groups.name: sandbox_escalation_channel_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no product feature that upgrades a running Unix sandbox through a datagram policy server or execve wrapper. Permission changes must continue through Ace approvals and a new launch rather than an in-sandbox escalation channel.
review_triggers: A running sandbox can request additional OS privileges without a new Ace launch.
An execve wrapper, escalation socket, or escalation policy daemon is added.

disposition_groups.name: execpolicy_starlark_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace does not use the Codex execpolicy Starlark language or its banned-prefix migration format. Ace approval-policy and rule-store behavior remains APPLICABLE under the existing PERM/EXEC/ACE controls.
review_triggers: Ace adopts Starlark or another executable command-policy language.
Ace imports or migrates Codex execpolicy configuration.

disposition_groups.name: managed_cloud_config_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace is not adding a cloud-delivered managed-configuration bundle, cache, identity, or refresh service. Local configuration integrity and fail-closed loading remain separately APPLICABLE.
review_triggers: Configuration is fetched from a remote policy service.
A managed bundle cache, tenant policy identity, expiry, HMAC, or background refresh is added.

disposition_groups.name: cloud_agent_identity_local_equivalents
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not add the Codex cloud agent-identity service. The transferable requirements are tracked through Ace owner/session identity, replay resistance, rotation, revocation, and recovery boundaries.
review_triggers: Ace begins signing remote task assertions or registering device/agent identities.
Ace introduces a remote agent identity endpoint, JWKS, or revocation registry.

disposition_groups.name: cloud_agent_key_local_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no Codex agent signing key, but CSPRNG generation and protected local identity-key storage remain requirements for Ace Gateway/session credentials.
review_triggers: Ace adds an Ed25519 or other asymmetric agent identity key.
Ace changes how Gateway/session identity keys are generated or stored.

disposition_groups.name: cloud_agent_jwks_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no cloud agent assertion format or JWKS issuer/audience trust domain. Ordinary Gateway authentication remains in scope under SEC/IPC/ACE IDs and is not made N/A.
review_triggers: Ace accepts JWT/JWKS agent assertions.
An issuer/audience-based remote agent trust domain is introduced.

disposition_groups.name: vendor_cloud_clients_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace is not adding Codex's AWS signing client, ChatGPT backend account client, or responses-api-proxy. Generic credential storage, host binding, stdin/argv secrecy, and provider security remain APPLICABLE under CRED/SEC/NET.
evidence: crew/providers/ and crew/gateway/ (Ace-native provider and Gateway paths)
review_triggers: Ace introduces AWS request signing, a ChatGPT-account backend client, or a responses API credential proxy.
A vendor-specific cloud credential transport is added.

disposition_groups.name: workload_identity_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no workload-identity assertion file or token-exchange product surface and will not add one as part of this security program. Existing credential and remote-auth controls remain separately APPLICABLE.
review_triggers: Ace accepts workload identity assertions from files or environment configuration.
Ace adds OAuth token exchange, federation, or cloud workload credentials.

disposition_groups.name: codex_code_mode_absent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex Code Mode, nested tools, transports, and V8 runtime
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not add Codex Code Mode, a model-controlled JavaScript runtime, nested-tool host, or Code Mode stdio/WebSocket/gRPC transport. Ordinary Ace tool execution remains APPLICABLE under EXEC/PROC/ACE.
evidence: crew/tools/ and crew/agent/loop/ (direct Ace tool routing, not Code Mode)
review_triggers: A model-controlled JavaScript/V8 runtime or nested-tool execution host is added.
A Code Mode stdio, WebSocket, or gRPC listener/transport appears.

disposition_groups.name: codex_style_inbound_mcp_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not add a Codex-style inbound MCP tool that starts arbitrary agent runs or lets callers override model, cwd, approval, sandbox, instructions, analytics, or arbitrary config. The existing owner-scoped Crew session MCP and token-bound interaction proxy are exact, enumerated exceptions and do not make this Codex surface applicable.
review_triggers: A new production MCPServer/FastMCP constructor or inbound MCP module is added.
The allowed Crew MCP servers accept model, cwd, approval, sandbox, arbitrary config, or unrestricted command execution.

disposition_groups.name: noise_remote_transport_absent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex Noise/ML-KEM rendezvous and remote-control product
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not add Codex's remote-execution relay, Noise hybrid transport, registry-authorized rendezvous bundle, harness-key validation, segmented remote-control stream, or remote client registry. Production Gateway is fail-closed to loopback and the native runtime uses private local stdio; Ace Gateway/runtime/channel authentication remains separately APPLICABLE.
evidence: crew/gateway/ and crew/security/runtime_client.py (Ace protocols without Noise)
review_triggers: Ace introduces Noise, ML-KEM, rendezvous bundles, harness keys, or a remote-control client registry.
Ace adds a segmented remote-control transport, non-loopback execution listener, or relay distinct from existing local Gateway messages.

disposition_groups.name: remote_stream_local_equivalent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex remote event sequencing and bounded stream lifecycle
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no Codex remote-control product, but sequence, replay, gap, backpressure, disconnect, and state-release requirements transfer to Ace Gateway/session streams.
review_triggers: Gateway replay/sequence semantics change.
Ace adds another remote event or response-body stream.

disposition_groups.name: stdio_to_uds_bridge_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no stdio-to-UDS forwarding product whose only authorization is socket-directory access. Existing loopback Gateway and stdio MCP paths keep their own authentication and lifecycle requirements.
review_triggers: A stdio-to-UDS or generic local socket forwarding bridge is added.
A local IPC bridge relies only on directory possession without an Ace identity check.

disposition_groups.name: local_endpoint_protection_equivalent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex UDS directory ownership and symlink protection
disposition_groups.reason: Ace uses authenticated loopback Gateway/session endpoints rather than the Codex UDS directory, so local endpoint ownership, key protection, symlink/reparse resistance, and cleanup are tracked through Ace's local identity and lifecycle IDs.
review_triggers: Ace changes its local listener or endpoint storage model.
Ace adds a Unix-domain socket or named-pipe control endpoint.

disposition_groups.name: daemon_updater_desktop_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not add the Codex Unix app-server-daemon or pipe downloaded installers to /bin/sh. Update-source, signature, rollback, bounded download, cleanup, and artifact provenance requirements are tracked against the existing Ace Desktop updater.
review_triggers: Ace adds a daemon/self-updater outside the Desktop updater.
Any update path executes downloaded script text or changes signature/rollback behavior.

disposition_groups.name: interactive_pty_product_absent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace exposes bounded pipe-based command execution and does not expose a PTY/ConPTY allocation, resize, or interactive terminal API. Pipe decoding, ANSI stripping, output budgets, cancellation, and process-tree cleanup remain independently APPLICABLE.
review_triggers: Ace adds PTY/ConPTY allocation, resize, terminal emulation, or interactive byte streaming.
A process API begins accepting a pty=true or terminal-mode option.

disposition_groups.name: tls_mitm_credential_injection_absent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex TLS MITM credential injection and managed CA
disposition_groups.reason: Ace deliberately uses policy-enforced transparent CONNECT/SNI tunnels and does not decrypt TLS, inject credentials into HTTPS requests, create a MITM CA, or mutate trust stores. Host/port/protocol authorization, DNS pinning, private-address denial, tunnel lifetime, and credential secrecy remain APPLICABLE.
review_triggers: Ace decrypts TLS, inspects HTTPS paths, injects request credentials, or creates a managed CA.
Any sandbox or browser profile begins receiving a product-managed CA or trust-store mutation.

disposition_groups.name: rollout_redaction_session_equivalent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex remote redaction versus persisted rollout
disposition_groups.reason: Ace does not use Codex rollout storage, but response redaction must not be confused with deletion of Ace session, task, audit, or checkpoint data.
review_triggers: Ace changes session redaction, deletion, export, or retention behavior.
A remote response-redaction layer is introduced.

disposition_groups.name: proxy_diagnostic_redaction_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has no Codex feedback envelope, but proxy and credential values must remain absent from Ace logs, diagnostics, subprocess environments, and exported evidence.
review_triggers: Ace adds diagnostic export, support bundles, or proxy configuration logging.
The inherited-environment allowlist or redaction pipeline changes.

disposition_groups.name: codex_cloud_product_docs_absent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex cloud environments and Codex Security/Trusted Access products
disposition_groups.reason: Ace is not adding Codex cloud setup/agent stages, cloud secret injection, Codex Security scanning service, or Trusted Access governance. Local network, secret, sandbox, and review controls remain separately APPLICABLE.
review_triggers: Ace gains hosted setup/agent environments or stage-specific cloud secret injection.
Ace adds a cloud security scanner, Trusted Access, entitlement, or cloud remediation service.

disposition_groups.name: plugin_governance_product_equivalent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex plugin availability and source-system permissions
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not copy Codex cloud plugin governance, but plugin/MCP source permissions, action confirmation, global configuration RBAC, domain binding, and audit requirements apply to Ace's existing plugin and MCP products.
review_triggers: Plugin/MCP installation, source authentication, action confirmation, or RBAC changes.
Ace adds a connector catalog, sync service, or remote plugin governance layer.

disposition_groups.name: skill_governance_product_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace already has skills and must enforce source, owner, inherited permissions, disablement, and cache invalidation through the Ace execution-surface and dangerous-mode controls rather than adding Codex cloud skill governance.
review_triggers: Skill discovery, installation, trust source, caching, or execution inheritance changes.
Ace introduces remote/workspace-managed skill distribution.

disposition_groups.name: browser_product_equivalent
disposition_groups.surface: Codex Browser and full CDP governance
disposition_groups.reason: Ace has its own Electron/Chromium Browser and CDP surface. Browser profile, page trust, downloads, local/internal access, sensitive CDP approval, admin policy, owner binding, and cleanup are tracked against the Ace Browser boundary.
review_triggers: Browser profile, navigation, download, upload, permission, or CDP behavior changes.
A new browser host or browser automation transport is added.

disposition_groups.name: computer_use_product_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace already has CUA/external-agent adapters. OS application scope, dangerous-action confirmation, file/network/process inheritance, revocation, and compatibility behavior are tracked against the Ace CUA boundary.
review_triggers: CUA installation, daemon, external-agent adapter, or OS permission behavior changes.
Ace adds another computer-control backend.

disposition_groups.name: remote_connection_product_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace will not add Codex Remote Connections, but remote owner authentication, host/session changes, revocation, approval replay, disconnect cleanup, and background process lifecycle apply to Ace Gateway sessions.
review_triggers: Remote authentication, reconnect, replay, revocation, or session lifecycle changes.
Ace adds remote host/device registration.

disposition_groups.name: compliance_audit_product_equivalent
disposition_groups.reason: Ace is not adding a cloud Compliance API, but append-only semantics, tenant-scoped query authorization, tamper resistance, retention, pagination, and export controls remain requirements for Ace's local security audit product.
review_triggers: Audit persistence, deletion, query, export, tenancy, or retention changes.
Ace adds a remote compliance/audit API.

required_stronger_negative.reason: The Codex standalone apply-patch alias runs without the session sandbox. Ace must prove that no patch/write alias or alternate entry can bypass its file authorization boundary.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: Enumerate every Ace patch/write entry and prove alias, direct-module, malformed argv, and missing-security-context calls deny before filesystem mutation.

required_stronger_negative.reason: Authentication failure changing the network route is a transferable fail-open pattern even though Ace has no cloud-tasks product.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: For every authenticated Ace outbound client, force missing/invalid credentials and prove it neither switches to a default/direct proxy route nor sends the request.

required_stronger_negative.reason: Unsupported allow output continuing the original tool input is a generic authorization fail-open risk, not a hook-product exemption.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: Malformed, unknown, incomplete, and unsupported permission decisions must deny; prove the original and updated tool inputs are both not executed.

required_stronger_negative.reason: A profile combination silently skipping the filesystem sandbox is a cross-product policy-composition risk.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: Exercise every Ace Linux permission/network profile combination and prove required filesystem, process, and network boundaries are never skipped without an explicit dangerous mode.

required_stronger_negative.reason: An existing proxy address must not suppress private/non-public target validation at the final connection point.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: Inject explicit proxy routing for Web, MCP, Browser, updater, and managed runtime traffic; private, loopback, link-local, and rebinding targets must still deny.

required_stronger_negative.reason: Falling back to an unverified original cwd after junction preparation failure is a transferable path-identity fail-open risk.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: Force Windows cwd canonicalization/junction/reparse preparation failures and prove Ace denies before process launch rather than using the original path.

required_stronger_negative.reason: Treating WFP installation failure as non-fatal can turn restricted networking into direct host networking.
required_stronger_negative.required_negative_test: Force every WFP setup/install/verification failure and prove managed-network launch is unavailable, no child starts, and no direct connection occurs.

absence_rules.description: No caller-selectable ExternalSandbox policy or bypass mode.
No in-sandbox escalation server or execve wrapper.
No Codex execpolicy or Starlark policy engine.
No Codex cloud config/tasks, workload identity, or vendor cloud identity client.
No Codex Code Mode host/runtime/protocol or jitless model runtime.
Only the existing Crew session MCP and bound interaction proxy may construct production MCP servers.
No non-loopback remote-execution listener, relay, or plaintext downgrade transport.
No Noise/ML-KEM rendezvous or harness-key remote-control transport.
No Codex app-server-daemon or downloaded-script shell updater.
No PTY/ConPTY allocation, resize, or interactive terminal API.
No TLS interception, HTTPS credential-injection hook, managed MITM CA, or trust-store mutation.
No Codex Security or Trusted Access cloud product implementation.
No cloud Compliance API or remote audit-export product.
